repos.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
repos.readme:
### The open protocol that connects any agent to any app. **[Docs](https://docs.ag-ui.com)** · **[Examples](https://dojo.ag-ui.com)** · **[Spec](https://docs.ag-ui.com/spec/1.0)** · **[Discord](https://discord.gg/Jd3FzfdJa8)**

**AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.** Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack. > [!IMPORTANT] > **AG-UI 1.0 is here.** The protocol now has a stable, frozen [specification](https://docs.ag-ui.com/spec/1.0) backed by a JSON Schema, and the TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs are generated from it. 1.0 is backwards compatible in both directions: 0.x agents work with 1.0 clients and vice versa. [What changed →](https://docs.ag-ui.com/spec/1.0/changelog) · [Migration guide →](https://docs.ag-ui.com/migrating-to-1-0) ## Quick start **Start a new app.** The CLI scaffolds a frontend ([CopilotKit](https://github.com/CopilotKit/CopilotKit) on Next.js, or a terminal client) wired to the agent framework you pick: ```bash npx create-ag-ui-app@latest ``` Then follow the printed next steps. The generated templates call OpenAI, so set your key before `npm run dev`: ```bash export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..." ```
Or speak the protocol directly: a 30-line agent server and client
An AG-UI agent is any HTTP endpoint that accepts a `RunAgentInput` and streams events back. No API keys needed for this one. **1. The agent (Python).** Requires Python 3.9+. ```bash pip install ag-ui-protocol fastapi uvicorn ``` ```python # server.py import uuid from fastapi import FastAPI, Request from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse from ag_ui.core import ( PROTOCOL_VERSION, RunAgentInput, RunStartedEvent, RunFinishedEvent, TextMessageStartEvent, TextMessageContentEvent, TextMessageEndEvent, ) from ag_ui.encoder import EventEncoder app = FastAPI() @app.post("/") async def run_agent(input_data: RunAgentInput, request: Request): encoder = EventEncoder(accept=request.headers.get("accept")) async def events(): yield encoder.encode(RunStartedEvent( thread_id=input_data.thread_id, run_id=input_data.run_id, protocol_version=PROTOCOL_VERSION, )) message_id = str(uuid.uuid4()) yield encoder.encode(TextMessageStartEvent(message_id=message_id, role="assistant")) for chunk in ["Hello ", "from ", "AG-UI!"]: yield encoder.encode(TextMessageContentEvent(message_id=message_id, delta=chunk)) yield encoder.encode(TextMessageEndEvent(message_id=message_id)) yield encoder.encode(RunFinishedEvent(thread_id=input_data.thread_id, run_id=input_data.run_id)) return StreamingResponse(events(), media_type=encoder.get_content_type()) ``` ```bash uvicorn server:app --port 8000 ``` **2. The client (TypeScript).** In a second terminal, in a new folder. Requires Node.js 20+. ```bash npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module npm install @ag-ui/client tsx ``` ```ts // client.ts import { HttpAgent } from "@ag-ui/client"; const agent = new HttpAgent({ url: "http://localhost:8000/" }); agent.addMessage({ id: crypto.randomUUID(), role: "user", content: "Hi there!" }); await agent.runAgent({}, { onRunStartedEvent: ({ event }) => console.log(`run started (AG-UI ${event.protocolVersion})`), onTextMessageContentEvent: ({ event }) => { process.stdout.write(event.delta); }, onRunFinishedEvent: () => console.log("\nrun finished"), }); ``` ```bash npx tsx client.ts ``` You should see `Hello from AG-UI!` stream in. Inbox Surface • Artifacts • Code Review

# Plannotator **⭐️ NEW:** [Plannotator Inbox](https://plannotator.ai/inbox/) is the missing review layer between you and multi-agent work. It surfaces decisions, prototypes, variations, plans, and everything you need to stay in the loop. Works with all coding agents and personal assistants. Plannotator is a local, browser-based review surface for AI coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, Droid, Amp, DeepSeek Harness, and Pi. Plannotator Inbox also works with personal assistants (Grok Bot, Muse, Hermes, OpenClaw). **It plugs directly into your agent** through plugins, hooks and commands. When the agent proposes a decision, plan, html, or finishes working, the app opens in your browser and you mark it up, comment, and send feedback directly to the agent for it to act on it.
### Review documents, plans, and agent messages Annotate plans, specs, messages, html, then send the feedback to your agent.
### Code Review Review local changes or remote PRs. Comment on diffs, suggest code. Your comments go back to the agent. Works with Git, GitButler, Jujutsu (`jj`), Perforce (`p4`), GitHub, and GitLab. For a big change, start a [guided review](https://plannotator.ai/code-review#guided-review): an agent sorts the diff into chapters, the most important first.
## Plannotator Inbox

Watch the demo · More on the Inbox · Docs

The Plannotator Inbox is one local window where your agents leave you messages, questions, files, and guided reviews while they keep working. Answer a question with a click, annotate a file, and press Send when you can. Nothing holds an agent session open while you do, and your reply goes back to the session that asked. ``` plannotator inbox ``` Claude Code, Pi, and OpenCode connect through Plannotator's plugins, and your replies arrive as their next turn. # Claude Trading Skills

**Data handling:** [Privacy policy](docs/en/privacy.md) · [Security policy](SECURITY.md)

Claude Trading Skills started as a personal project to use AI to improve my own trading process.

Claude Trading Skills is a Claude Skills-based trading workflow toolkit for time-constrained individual investors.

It is designed for investors who use long-term investing, ETFs, and dividend stocks as their core, while using disciplined swing trading as a satellite strategy when market conditions are favorable.

The goal is not to outsource buy/sell decisions to AI. The goal is to structure market review, risk management, trade planning, journaling, and continuous improvement. It is open source because the workflows, checklists, and review habits behind better trading decisions can improve through shared practice.

This is not a signal service or a promise of profitability. It is a toolkit for traders who want to build a better decision process.

The project follows a **first for self, open for others** stance: it is built first as a practical workflow the author uses, then shared openly for others who face similar constraints.

📖 **Documentation site:** <https://tradermonty.github.io/claude-trading-skills/>

**Project vision:** [`PROJECT_VISION.md`](PROJECT_VISION.md)

日本語版READMEは[`README.ja.md`](README.ja.md)をご覧ください。

## Disclaimer

This repository is for educational, research, and process-improvement purposes only. It is not financial advice, investment advisory service, tax advice, legal advice, a signal service, or a broker execution platform. Trading and investing involve risk, including loss of principal. Past performance, backtests, screens, reports, and AI-generated analysis do not guarantee future results. All trading decisions, position sizing, tax/regulatory compliance, and broker usage are the user's responsibility.

The project is provided under the MIT License, **AS IS, WITHOUT WARRANTY**.

## Who This Is For

This repository is designed for:

- Time-constrained individual investors
- Long-term investors who also want disciplined swing-trading upside
- Dividend and ETF investors who want structured portfolio review
- Traders who want to manage risk before finding trade candidates
- Investors who want to journal and improve their decision process

It is not designed for fully automated trading, signal outsourcing, or short-term scalping.

## Recommended Starting Path

New users should start with one of these operational workflows. Each link points to a machine-readable manifest under [`workflows/`](workflows/) that names the exact skills, decision gates, and artifacts in order.

| Goal | Workflow | Anchor Skills | API Profile |

| Record and learn from every closed trade | [`trade-memory-loop`](workflows/trade-memory-loop.yaml) | trader-memory-core, signal-postmortem | No API for manual path |
| Review monthly performance and adjust rules | [`monthly-performance-review`](workflows/monthly-performance-review.yaml) ([sample](examples/workflows/monthly-performance-review/sample-run/)) | trader-memory-core, signal-postmortem, backtest-expert | No API for manual path |

New here? Follow [Your First Week](docs/en/your-first-week.md) ([日本語](docs/ja/your-first-week.md)) from installation through a no-paid-data-API market check, first journal entry, and first weekly review.

# Chronicles of the Realm · 江山时序

**An Interactive Historical Atlas of China from the Warring States (403 BCE) to the Present — Scrub Through Time, Trace Ancient Cities, and Walk in the Footsteps of History** [**Play Live Demo (English UI) → https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en**](https://deanchen.me/jiangshan-map/?lang=en) *The story behind it (in Chinese): [From textbook maps to 1k GitHub stars](https://deanchen.me/history/atlas/2026/10/25/jiangshan-map-story.html)*

--- ## Why It's Fun to Explore Have you ever wondered while reading Chinese history or classical poetry: - *"Where exactly on today's map are Jiankang (the Six Dynasties capital), Huangzhou (where Su Dongpo composed the Red Cliffs Rhapsody in exile), Languan Pass in the Qinling Mountains (where Han Yu halted his horse in the snow), or Zhuxianzhen (Yue Fei's northern campaign frontier)?"* - *"How many names did Chang'an hold across two millennia, and what pivotal events unfolded on that soil?"* - *"How did the realm evolve step by step—from the Partition of Jin and the Seven Warring States at the opening of Sima Guang's Zizhi Tongjian (403 BCE), Qin's unification campaigns, Emperor Wu of Han opening the Hexi Corridor, High Tang's Four Garrisons of Anxi, and Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan jurisdiction over Tibet, to Zeng Jize's recovery of Ili (1881 CE) and the 20th-century shift from the 'Begonia Leaf' (秋海棠) map to the 'Rooster' (雄鸡) map?"* **Chronicles of the Realm (`jiangshan-map`)** brings together **2,400+ years** of Chinese history across **18 historical periods** into a single interactive parchment atlas—featuring **multi-stage territorial and prefecture snapshots**, **ancient cities**, **strategic mountain passes**, **poetic and battlefield landmarks**, **chronological milestones**, and **reigning monarchs & imperial eras**. No heavy print atlases required—just drag the timeline and click any city to travel through space and time. --- ### Feature 1: Scrub the Timeline to Watch Realms Rise & Fall, Track Monarchs, and Compare Ancient & Modern Borders - **Multi-Polity Confrontations on a Single Canvas**: From the Seven Warring States (Qin, Chu, Qi, Yan, Zhao, Wei, Han) alongside Zhou, Yue, Ba-Shu, Zhongshan, and Yiqu, to the Three Kingdoms warlords (Yuan Shao, Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Sun Quan, Gongsun's Liaodong), Northern & Southern Dynasties, Five Dynasties & Ten Kingdoms, and Song, Liao, Western Xia, Dali, Jin, and the Mongols—all rendered side-by-side in high-contrast traditional parchment hues. Hover over any polity in the bottom-left legend to highlight its territory, or click to open that polity's profile (lifespan, capitals and a short history) and zoom to its territory. - **Multi-Stage Territorial Evolution & Dashed "Ghost Boundary Diffs"**: At every major territorial milestone—such as Qin's conquest of Ba-Shu (316 BCE), Yan General Qin Kai's expansion into Liaodong (300 BCE), Ma Yuan's bronze pillars in Jiaozhi (43 CE), Sima Yi's campaign in Liaodong (238 CE), Li Jing's conquest of Tuyuhun (635 CE), the Four Garrisons of Anxi & Wang Xuance's campaign in Central India (648 CE), Yuan's Xuanzhengyuan rule over Tibet (1288 CE), Ming's Jiaozhi Province in Annam (1407 CE), the 1881 Treaty of Saint Petersburg recovering Ili, the 1898 foreign leased territories, the 1945 retrocession of Taiwan, and the 1946 transition from the **"Begonia Leaf" (秋海棠)** map to the **"Rooster" (雄鸡)** map—click any milestone or phase dot to switch maps and reveal the previous phase's dashed vermilion **Ghost Boundary Diff** so territorial gains and losses are immediately visible. - **Reigning Monarch on the Timeline**: The bubble above the timeline names the monarch on the throne in the current year (e.g. `100 BCE · Western Han · Emp. Wu`, `630 CE · Tang · Emp. Taizong`, `1700 CE · Qing · Kangxi Emp. (Shengzu)`); the Chinese interface also shows the regnal era year (`唐太宗·贞观四年`). - **Ancient Prefecture Hover Inspection & Modern Province Overlay**: First-level administrative divisions (Commanderies, Circuits, Routes, and Provinces) are rendered with deduplicated **Parchment Casing** borders. Zoom in and hover over any prefecture (e.g., Ming `Yingtian Prefecture` or Three Kingdoms `Jingzhou`) to inspect its jurisdiction and modern provincial equivalents. # Stitch Design Skills A collection of agent skills and plugins for [Google Stitch](https://stitch.withgoogle.com), following the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) open standard. Compatible with coding agents such as Codex, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode (manual install). ## Quick Start ### 1. Install Plugins (Recommended) The fastest way to set up the full Stitch plugin suite globally. #### Codex Add the Stitch Skills marketplace, then install the plugins you need.
Via CLI (recommended) ```bash codex plugin marketplace add google-labs-code/stitch-skills --ref main \ --sparse .agents/plugins \ --sparse plugins/stitch-design \ --sparse plugins/stitch-build \ --sparse plugins/stitch-utilities ``` > [!TIP] > The `--sparse` flags are optional — they limit the checkout to only the > listed paths for a faster clone. **An AI agent-led search engine scored by upvotes, likes, and real money - not editors.** This README tracks the current v4 pipeline. The runtime skill spec lives in [skills/last30days/SKILL.md](skills/last30days/SKILL.md), which is the source of truth for the latest command and setup behavior. **Claude Code (recommended — auto-updates via marketplace):** ``` /plugin marketplace add mvanhorn/last30days-skill /plugin install last30days ``` **Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, or any of 50+ [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) hosts:** ``` npx skills add mvanhorn/last30days-skill -g ``` (`-g` installs globally for your user, available across all projects. Drop it to scope per-project.) More install options (claude.ai web, OpenClaw, manual) in the [Install](#install) section below. Zero config. Reddit, HN, Polymarket, and GitHub work immediately. Run it once and the setup wizard unlocks X, YouTube, TikTok, arXiv, Techmeme, and more in 30 seconds. --- Reddit upvotes. X likes. YouTube transcripts. TikTok engagement. Polymarket odds backed by real money and insider information. That's millions of people voting with their attention and their wallets every day. /last30days searches all of it in parallel, scores it by what real people actually engage with, and an AI agent judge synthesizes it into one brief. Google aggregates editors. /last30days searches people. You can't get this search anywhere else because no single AI has access to all of it. Google search doesn't touch Reddit comments or X posts. ChatGPT has a deal with Reddit but can't search X or TikTok. Gemini has YouTube but not Reddit. Claude has none of them natively. Each platform is a walled garden with its own API, its own tokens, its own auth. But you can bring your own keys and browser sessions, and suddenly an AI agent can search all of them at once, score them against each other, and tell you what actually matters. That's the unlock. Not one better search engine. A dozen disconnected platforms, bridged by an agent. ``` /last30days Peter Steinberger ``` You have a meeting tomorrow. You Google them. You get their LinkedIn from 2023. /last30days gives you what they're actually doing this month: joined OpenAI to work on Codex, fighting Anthropic's ban on third-party agents, shipping 23 PRs at 85% merge rate, building "LobsterOS" for cross-device agent control, and r/ClaudeCode hit 569 upvotes debating whether he's a hero or "insufferable." Scattered across X posts, Reddit threads, YouTube transcripts, and GitHub commits. None of it was on Google. ## Why this exists I built it to keep up in AI. Everything changes every day and the Reddit and X nerds are always on top of it first. I needed better prompts, and the training data was always months behind what the community had already figured out. But it turned into something bigger. Now I run it before a sales call to know the last 30 days truth about a business. Before a meeting to read someone's recent tweets and podcast transcripts. Before a Disney World trip to know which rides are closed and what the community says about Genie+. Before I build anything to know what problems people are actually hitting. # SkillEvaluator ![SkillEvaluator wordmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/ad2815fe78c045db91d230681d32863698da08cf/docs/assets/skillevaluator-wordmark.svg) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache%202.0-green.svg)](LICENSE) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/Python-3.12%20%7C%203.13%20%7C%203.14-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/skillevaluator.svg?label=PyPI)](https://pypi.org/project/skillevaluator/) [![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/Documentation-docs.nvidia.com-blue.svg)](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/) [![Paper](https://img.shields.io/badge/arXiv-2608.20614-b31b1b.svg)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20614) [![NVIDIA Developer Blog](https://img.shields.io/badge/Blog-NVIDIA%20Developer-76B900.svg)](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/evaluating-ai-agent-skill-performance-with-nvidia-skillevaluator/) > 📺 **Livestream:** [Ask the Experts: Evaluating Agent Skills](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4rI0zATFxYI) SkillEvaluator checks AI agent skills and measures their effect on task results: start with quality checks, then compare runs with and without a skill. Agent skills are folders of instructions and supporting files defined by the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/). SkillEvaluator is part of the [NVIDIA Verified Skills pipeline](https://github.com/NVIDIA/skills). ## Get started Three ways in, one CLI, same results.
1. Run the CLI directly 2. Add it to your repo via CI 3. Wire it to your agent
Install with pip: ```bash pip install skillevaluator ```
Or install with uv ```bash uv tool install \ skillevaluator ```
Then check your skill, no API key: ```bash skillevaluator validate \ ./my-skill --tiers 1 ``` Other tiers: [installation guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation). 		Our CI template checks every skill change. No evaluation code to maintain. Run this in your GitHub repository. It opens a setup PR: ```bash skillevaluator ci init ``` GitLab and details: [repository guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/repository-integration). Add the skill to Claude Code, Codex or another agent: ```bash npx skills add \ NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator ``` Then ask: *"Is my skill any good?"* See the [agent guide](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/agent-skill).
## Quickstart Both paths use bundled `text-analyzer`. | Start here | Requires | First result | | --- | --- | --- | | [Run without an LLM](#run-without-an-llm) | Git and uv | A deterministic quality score and findings | | [Use NVIDIA Build](#use-nvidia-build) | Git, uv, and a Build API key | Model-backed rubric scores and feedback | Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and Git, then get the example: ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator.git cd SkillEvaluator ``` uv provisions Python 3.13 and dependencies. For standalone installation, see [Installation](https://docs.nvidia.com/skills/skillevaluator/installation). ### Run without an LLM ```bash uv run --python 3.13 skillevaluator quality-check \ src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \ -r cli -r json -o reports/first-quality ``` No API key, scanner, GPU or Docker is needed. The example scores **88.8/100 (B)**, exits `0` and saves `reports/first-quality/skillevaluator-quality.json`. The passing threshold defaults to 70. This checks static quality; publication evidence stays `INCOMPLETE`. Security needs scanners; agent impact needs live evaluation. Replace the example path with your skill directory. See the [keyless walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#run-without-an-llm). ### Use NVIDIA Build Eligible NVIDIA Developer Program members can use NVIDIA-hosted endpoints for **free prototyping**, subject to [access terms and rate limits](https://docs.api.nvidia.com/nim/docs/product). 1. Sign in at [build.nvidia.com](https://build.nvidia.com/) and complete enrollment. 2. Open a model page, select **Get API Key**, and generate your key. 3. Set the provider and key in the same terminal, then run the rubric check: ```bash export SKILL_EVAL_LLM_PROVIDER=nv_build export NVIDIA_API_KEY='nvapi-...' uv run --python 3.13 --extra llm skillevaluator rubric-eval \ src/skillevaluator/tier3/reference_skills/text-analyzer \ -r cli -r json -o reports/first-build ``` The command sends skill documentation to the model and saves feedback in `reports/first-build/skillevaluator-rubric.json`. No agent runtime or Docker is needed. Completed evaluations can still fail rubric thresholds. The same key supports Tier 2 embeddings and supported Tier 3 agents. See the [Build walkthrough](docs/quickstart.mdx#use-nvidia-build) or [provider configuration](docs/configuration.mdx). ## Three-tier overview ![SkillEvaluator three-tier pipeline: Skill → Tier 1 Validation → Tier 2 Deduplication → Tier 3 Live Evaluation → Reports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NVIDIA/SkillEvaluator/ad2815fe78c045db91d230681d32863698da08cf/docs/assets/three-tier-overview.svg) Each tier is independent. --- ## What is Open Code Review? Open Code Review is an AI-powered code review CLI tool. It originated as Alibaba Group's internal official AI code review assistant — over the past two years, it has served tens of thousands of developers and identified millions of code defects. After thorough validation at massive scale, we incubated it into an open source project for the community. Simply configure a model endpoint to get started. It reads Git diffs, sends changed files to a configurable LLM via an agent with tool-use capabilities, and generates structured review comments with line-level precision. The agent can read full file contents, search the codebase, inspect other changed files for context, and produce deep reviews — not just surface-level diff feedback. Beyond diff review, `ocr scan` reviews entire files for auditing unfamiliar codebases or directories that have no meaningful diff. Visit the [official website](https://open-codereview.ai) for more details. ![Highlights](imgs/highlights-en.png) ## Benchmark > Compared to general-purpose agents (Claude Code), Open Code Review achieves significantly higher **Precision** and **F1** with the same underlying model, while consuming only **~1/9 of the tokens** and completing reviews faster. Note that its Recall is lower than general-purpose agents — a deliberate trade-off favoring precision over noise. A real-world code review benchmark built from **50** popular open-source repositories, **200** real Pull Requests, and **10** programming languages — cross-validated by 80+ senior engineers (**1,505** annotated ground-truth issues). #
🎻 PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing
Yiwen Song1, Yale Song1, Tomas Pfister1, and Jinsung Yoon1
1Google Cloud AI Research


PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing. It flexibly transforms unconstrained pre-writing materials (ideas and experimental logs) into submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts, including comprehensive literature synthesis and generated visuals, such as plots and conceptual diagrams. Acting like an orchestrated team of specialized agents, it handles outline generation, literature review, section writing, content refinement, and plotting to close the gap between raw research materials and submission ready papers.
## Key Features - **Multi-Agent Pipeline**: Orchestrates specialized agents (Outline, Literature Review, Section Writing, Content Refinement, Plotting) for end-to-end paper generation. - **Comprehensive Literature Synthesis**: Automatically searches, prioritizes, and integrates relevant literature into the manuscript. - **Visuals Generation**: Generates plots and supports the inclusion of conceptual diagrams. - **LaTeX Automation**: Produces submission-ready LaTeX manuscripts adhering to target conference templates. ## Installation 1. **Environment Setup**: The project relies on a Conda environment named `paper_orchestra`. You can set up a similar environment with Python 3.11 and install the required dependencies. ```bash conda create -n paper_orchestra python=3.11 conda activate paper_orchestra pip install -r requirements.txt ``` 2. **Environment Variables**: Create a `.env` file in the root of the project and add your API keys: ```env # Add keys if you have them, otherwise leave them empty # You need to specify related keys if you want to use the model # For example, if you want to use Gemini models, you need to specify either VERTEX_AI_PROJECT and VERTEX_AI_LOCATION, or GEMINI_API_KEY # If you want to use OpenAI models, you need to specify OPENAI_API_KEY SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY=your_semantic_scholar_api_key OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_api_key VERTEX_AI_PROJECT=your_vertex_ai_project VERTEX_AI_LOCATION=your_vertex_ai_location GEMINI_API_KEY=your_gemini_api_key # if you want to run demo and send emails to yourself at the end, set these 2 fields as well SMTP_EMAIL=your_email SMTP_PASSWORD=your_password ``` ## Dataset The dataset used for paper generation is **not included** in this code repository. It will be released separately at a later date. Once available, you should download the dataset and place it under the `datasets/` directory. ## Usage You can run the paper generation pipeline using the provided bash script or directly via the Python CLI. ### Using the Bash Script ```bash ./paper_writing_cli.sh ``` ### Using the Python CLI directly ```bash python paper_writing_cli.py \ --raw_materials_dir /path_to_your_raw_materials/ \ --latex_template_dir /path_to_your_latex_template/ \ --output_dir /path_to_your_output_folder/ \ --use_plotting true ``` ### Key Arguments * `--raw_materials_dir`: (Required) Directory containing the raw materials (e.g., idea and experimental log). * `--latex_template_dir`: (Required) Directory containing the LaTeX template (e.g., `templates/cvpr2025`). * `--output_dir`: Directory to output the generated paper. If not specified, an automatic folder with a timestamp is created. * `--use_plotting`: Enable the plotting agent workflow to generate figures from code (Default: `False`). * `--writer_model_name`: LLM for writer and literature agents. * `--reflection_model_name`: LLM for reflection agents. ### Interactive Demo We provide an interactive Streamlit demo for the paper generation pipeline. For instructions on how to run and use it, please refer to the [README.md](frontend/README.md) in the `frontend` directory. ## Project Structure * `autoraters/`: Contains scripts for automated evaluation. * `methods/`: Core logic for agents and pipeline execution. * `templates/`: LaTeX templates for target conferences, you can add your own template by creating a new subfolder under this directory. * `utils/`: Utility functions for API calls, PDF handling, etc. ## Citation If you find this repo or our paper helpful, please cite it as follows: ```bibtex @article{song2026paperorchestra, title={PaperOrchestra: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated AI Research Paper Writing}, author={Song, Yiwen and Song, Yale and Pfister, Tomas and Yoon, Jinsung}, journal={arXiv preprint arXiv:2604.05018}, year={2026} } ``` # Disclaimer This is not an officially supported Google product.
